phase1.intro:
This is opening day for real — every piece from this unit, assembled into one working app.

Where should we start?

topics.buttonText: How does the Task class use properties to keep the stats live?
dialogue: The To-Do List app's Task class holds its data as properties (StringProperty, BooleanProperty, ObjectProperty<LocalDate>) instead of plain fields — that's what lets the stats label stay live via `Bindings.createStringBinding()`, the same binding pattern from 5.10, recalculating automatically every time the ObservableList changes.

stickyNote.flavor: 📊 property fields keep a stats label live automatically
stickyNote.definition: Using StringProperty/BooleanProperty/etc. fields (instead of plain fields) lets Bindings.createStringBinding() keep a stats label auto-updated.

topics.buttonText: What's the "single source of truth" pattern here?
dialogue: [[key:The pattern worth noticing is the separation between data and display]]: tasks (the ObservableList) is the single source of truth, and every visible control derives what it shows from that one list rather than tracking its own separate copy. Change the list, and everything downstream updates itself.

stickyNote.flavor: 🎯 the ObservableList is the one truth, everything else derives
stickyNote.definition: The ObservableList<Task> is the single source of truth; the ListView and stats label both derive their display from it rather than keeping separate copies.

topics.buttonText: Does this pattern apply beyond a to-do list?
dialogue: [[fun:The alternate CalculatorApp class at the bottom of the file]] uses the exact same toolkit — GridPane for the button grid, setOnAction() for every key — proving the pattern generalizes: once you've built one real JavaFX app, you've basically got the shape of all of them.

stickyNote.flavor: 🧮 same toolkit builds a calculator too
stickyNote.definition: The same JavaFX toolkit (layouts, controls, setOnAction, binding) used for the to-do app builds a calculator too — the shape of one real app transfers to most others.

phase1.output: (Full To-Do List application with add, complete, delete, and stats functionality)
phase1.openingDialogue: The mini-app assembles everything from this unit — properties feeding live bindings, one ObservableList as the single source of truth. 🎯

phase2.errorMessage: (Tasks are added to the data but the UI DOESN'T UPDATE!)
phase2.explanation:
[[warn:a task gets added to the underlying data, but the on-screen list doesn't change]] — the data is correct, the display just doesn't reflect it.

tasks.add(...) updates the ObservableList itself just fine. [[key:the missing piece is telling the ListView it needs to re-render]] — in this app's real version, that's updateTaskListView(), which calls listView.setItems(tasks) (or a refresh()) after every change. If a ListView's setItems() was only ever called once, early on, and the list reference itself never changes, some rendering paths can lag behind unless the view is explicitly told to look again. This is the same family of bug as 5.5's empty window and 5.11's blank table — a data step happened correctly, but the corresponding "now show it" step got skipped.

phase3.openingDialogue: Mini App — bring it all together! 🚀

mcq.question:
In the To-Do app, the statsLabel updates its "Total / Completed / Pending" text automatically every time a task is added, completed, or deleted — with no button, no manual refresh call anywhere near it. What mechanism makes that possible?

A) A background thread polling the task list every second
B) Bindings.createStringBinding(), which recomputes automatically whenever its ObservableList dependency changes
C) statsLabel has a built-in ListView listener by default
D) The label re-reads the list every time the window regains focus

phase4.selfChallenge:
Create a simple Contact Manager app with:
1. A TableView with columns: Name, Phone, Email
2. TextFields for adding new contacts
3. An "Add Contact" button that adds to the table
4. A "Delete Contact" button that removes the selected contact
5. Show the total number of contacts

Use ObservableList for data and PropertyValueFactory for columns.

phase5.trivia: [[warn:JavaFX ships its own class also named Task]] — javafx.concurrent.Task, used for running background work off the UI thread — which has nothing to do with this lesson's own Task model class for to-do items. Importing the wrong one is a genuinely easy mistake if you ever build a version of this app that loads tasks from a slow source in the background.
